text:
elaine: dropping an nsys trace from today's mixed-quant rollout. model used fp8 for long sequences, int8 for short. seeing a big GPU idle spike around step ~1200 and lots of HtoD activity. s3://redwood-traces/1778888888-mixed-quant.nsys.gz

sam: thanks — can you paste the top kernel timeline + any nvprof summary? want to see dequant / host memcpy contributions

elaine: quick excerpt from the nsys summary (trimmed):
```
KERNEL TIMELINE (excerpt)
conv1_fp8_qu8_forward: 12.3ms
dequantize_fp8_to_fp32: 5.8ms  <-- hot, happens on every token
packed_gemm_int8: 3.1ms
kv_read_kernel: 0.8ms
hostMemcpyAsync HtoD: 6.2ms  <-- correlates with idle gaps
hostMemcpyAsync DtoH: 0.4ms
```

matt: hostMemcpyAsync at 6.2ms per op is a red flag. NVTX shows it overlapping kernel waits — likely staging buffer fallback or non-pinned pages. also fp8 dequant on host looks expensive.

nathan: we rolled a batching heuristic change yesterday to favor lower latency (more smaller microbatches). could be increasing relative overhead of dequant/hostcopy per request.

elaine: we also changed the quant routing policy: prefer int8 for seq<=64, fp8 for seq>64. maybe policy flipflops for mid-length traffic and causes extra dequant roundtrips when model variants are switched.

sam: can you run a perfetto capture with gpu_compute + gpu_memcpy tracks so we can visually confirm memcpy vs kernel gaps? also include nvtx markers around cache ops.

tracebot: perfetto trace generated: https://perfetto.grafana.local/trace/1778888888 - shows HtoD bulk at 1203-1209 and kernel idle wedges at same interval

matt: suggestions: (1) try enabling pinned host buffers / cuMemHostRegister for the allocation path (2) add a microbench forcing int8 only and fp8 only to measure dequant overhead (3) instrument KV cache NVTX markers so we can see if KV spill triggers host roundtrips

elaine: ran quick microbench (synthetic workload):
```
bench config: seq=64, batch=8, 1000 iters
fp8 path: p50=18ms p95=42ms
int8 path: p50=12ms p95=28ms
measured dequant + hostcopy overhead (isolated): ~6.1ms per invocation
```

nathan: that matches theory: dequant + hostcopy is ~6ms which is huge for small requests. microbatching multiplies that cost.

sam: proposed action items:
- reproduce with synthetic load (elaine)
- rerun with pinned page pool enabled (matt)
- add NVTX around dequant + KV read ops (sam)
- test kernel warmup to keep KV cache on device (nathan)
- if still bad, change routing policy to prefer int8 for seq<=128 for a canary

elaine: i'll run 1-3 tonight and post updated traces. opened perf ticket PERF-2316 to track followups. cc @matt @sam @nathan

perf-bot: Perf ticket PERF-2316 created (priority P2). SLA 72h.

matt: also note: if pinned buffers fix it, we should add a heuristic to prefer pinned allocations for dequant staging buffers and measure memory overhead.

elaine: noted. i'll include allocation stats and nvprof summaries in the ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
